name: A4988 stepper motor driver
description: Allegro A4988 microstepping driver for one bipolar stepper motor: STEP/DIR control with a built-in translator, full to 1/16 step, adjustable current limit (trimpot, up to about 1 A per coil without cooling, 2 A with), motor supply 8-35 V, logic supply 3-5.5 V. Sold as: Pololu A4988 Stepper Motor Driver Carrier (#1182, and the many same-pinout clone modules), 16 pins in two rows: EN MS1 MS2 MS3 RST SLP STEP DIR, opposite side top to bottom VMOT GND 2B 2A 1A 1B VDD GND.
eli5: Turns a stepper motor exactly one small click every time your board sends it a pulse, in the direction you choose.

pins.name: EN
pins.description: ENABLE, active low: low = motor outputs on, high = outputs off (shaft free). 100 kOhm pull-down on the board, so it is enabled if left open

pins.name: MS1
pins.description: Microstep select 1 (100 kOhm pull-down in the chip). MS1/MS2/MS3: LLL full, HLL 1/2, LHL 1/4, HHL 1/8, HHH 1/16

pins.name: MS2
pins.description: Microstep select 2 (50 kOhm pull-down in the chip)

pins.name: MS3
pins.description: Microstep select 3 (100 kOhm pull-down in the chip)

pins.name: RST
pins.description: RESET, active low: must be HIGH for the driver to run. Floating on the board: drive it high from a GPIO or jumper it to SLP

pins.name: SLP
pins.description: SLEEP, active low: low = sleep (< 10 uA). 100 kOhm pull-up to VDD on the board, so it is awake if left open. Wait 1 ms after waking before stepping

pins.name: STEP
pins.description: STEP: each low-to-high edge moves the motor one (micro)step. Min 1 us high, 1 us low. No pull on the board: never leave floating

pins.name: DIR
pins.description: DIR: direction, read on each STEP rising edge. No pull on the board: never leave floating

pins.name: VMOT
pins.description: Motor supply 8-35 V from a separate supply (not the microcontroller), with a >= 47 uF electrolytic capacitor across VMOT/GND close to the board

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Motor supply ground (printed GND, next to VMOT): the return for the VMOT supply; joined to the logic GND on the board

pins.name: 1B
pins.description: Motor coil 1, second wire (OUT1B). Connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Logic supply 3-5.5 V. Logic high must be >= 0.7 x VDD, so use 3.3 V with a 3.3 V microcontroller

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Logic ground (printed GND, bottom pin next to VDD): connect to the microcontroller GND; joined to the motor GND on the board

buildNotes: Two supplies: logic VDD 3-5.5 V from the microcontroller (3.3 V for an ESP32/Pico, since logic high must be >= 0.7 x VDD) and motor VMOT 8-35 V from a separate supply. Join the grounds.
Put a 47 uF or larger electrolytic capacitor across VMOT and GND right at the board: the ceramic capacitors on it alone let voltage spikes exceed the 35 V rating.
RST floats on the board and the driver ignores STEP while it is low. Drive it high from a GPIO or jumper it to the neighbouring SLP pin (pulled up to VDD).
Never connect or disconnect the motor while VMOT is powered: it destroys the driver.

Set the current limit before running the motor: VREF (measured between the trimpot and GND) = 8 x I x Rcs. Pololu boards since 2017 have Rcs = 0.068 Ohm (1 A -> 0.54 V); many clones use 0.1 Ohm (1 A -> 0.8 V).
Microstepping (Table 1): MS1/MS2/MS3 = LLL full, HLL half, LHL quarter, HHL eighth, HHH sixteenth. Left open they read low (full step).
STEP pulses: at least 1 us high and 1 us low; change DIR at least 200 ns before the STEP rising edge. After SLP goes high wait 1 ms before stepping.
Above about 1 A per coil the chip needs a heat sink or airflow; it shuts down when it overheats.

driver.code:
# A4988 microstepping bipolar stepper driver (Allegro A4988), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Allegro A4988 datasheet (A4988-DS) and the Pololu A4988 carrier (#1182) schematic.
#   STEP: each LOW->HIGH edge moves the motor one (micro)step. Min HIGH pulse 1 us, min LOW 1 us (tA, tB).
#   DIR:  direction, sampled on the STEP rising edge. Setup/hold time to STEP: 200 ns (tC, tD).
#   RESET (RST, active low): low = translator to Home, all FET outputs off, STEP ignored. Must be HIGH to run.
#         The Pololu board leaves RST floating: drive it high from a GPIO (rst=) or jumper it to SLP.
#   SLEEP (SLP, active low): low = sleep. Board pull-up 100 kOhm to VDD. After waking, wait 1 ms before stepping.
#   ENABLE (EN, active low): high = all FET outputs off (motor free). Board pull-down 100 kOhm, so enabled if open.
#   MS1 MS2 MS3 (Table 1): LLL full, HLL 1/2, LHL 1/4, HHL 1/8, HHH 1/16. Internal pull-downs (full step if open).
#         A new step mode takes effect on the next STEP rising edge.
# Logic HIGH must be >= 0.7 x VDD: with a 3.3 V microcontroller power VDD from 3.3 V, not 5 V.
from machine import Pin
import time

_MODES = {1: (0, 0, 0), 2: (1, 0, 0), 4: (0, 1, 0), 8: (1, 1, 0), 16: (1, 1, 1)}


class A4988:
    def __init__(self, step, dir, rst=None, slp=None, en=None, ms=None):
        """step, dir: GPIO numbers wired to STEP and DIR (both needed; neither has a pull on the board).
        rst: GPIO wired to RST, or None if RST is jumpered to SLP. Driven high here.
        slp: GPIO wired to SLP, or None (board pull-up keeps it awake).
        en: GPIO wired to EN, or None (board pull-down keeps the outputs enabled).
        ms: (ms1, ms2, ms3) GPIO numbers, or None (full step via the internal pull-downs)."""
        self.step_pin = Pin(step, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.dir_pin = Pin(dir, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.en = Pin(en, Pin.OUT, value=0) if en is not None else None
        self.slp = Pin(slp, Pin.OUT, value=1) if slp is not None else None
        self.ms = [Pin(p, Pin.OUT, value=0) for p in ms] if ms is not None else None
        self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1) if rst is not None else None
        self.position = 0
        # Leaving reset / sleep: charge pump needs 1 ms before the first STEP (datasheet, Sleep Mode).
        time.sleep_ms(1)

    def set_microstep(self, div):
        """div = 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 (full, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth step). Needs ms= pins."""
        if self.ms is None:
            raise ValueError('MS1-MS3 not wired: board is fixed at full step')
        bits = _MODES[div]
        for p, b in zip(self.ms, bits):
            p.value(b)

    def direction(self, forward):
        """Set DIR (1 = forward). Takes effect on the next STEP rising edge."""
        self.dir_pin.value(1 if forward else 0)
        time.sleep_us(1)  # >= 200 ns setup before STEP

    def step(self, n, delay_us=1000):
        """Move n steps; n < 0 runs backwards. delay_us = time per step (>= 2, i.e. 1 us high + 1 us low)."""
        if n == 0:
            return
        self.direction(n > 0)
        half = max(1, delay_us // 2)
        s = self.step_pin
        for _ in range(abs(n)):
            s.value(1)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tA >= 1 us
            s.value(0)
            time.sleep_us(half)   # tB >= 1 us
        self.position += n

    def enable(self, on=True):
        """EN low = outputs on (motor holds torque); EN high = outputs off (shaft turns freely)."""
        if self.en is not None:
            self.en.value(0 if on else 1)

    def disable(self):
        self.enable(False)

    def sleep(self):
        """SLP low: outputs, regulator and charge pump off (< 10 uA)."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(0)

    def wake(self):
        """SLP high, then the 1 ms charge-pump start-up before stepping."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    def reset(self):
        """Pulse RST low: translator back to Home, outputs off while low."""
        if self.rst is not None:
            self.rst.value(0)
            time.sleep_us(10)
            self.rst.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(1)


def vref_for_current(amps, rcs=0.068):
    """VREF (volts, measured on the trimpot) for a current limit per coil: ITripMAX = VREF / (8 x Rcs).
    Pololu boards made since 2017 have Rcs = 0.068 Ohm (older green-resistor boards 0.050 Ohm).
    Clone boards often use 0.1 Ohm (R100): check the sense resistors on yours."""
    return 8 * amps * rcs

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from a4988 import A4988

# STEP/DIR to GPIOs, RST driven high (it floats on the board). Full step: MS1-MS3 left open.
motor = A4988({STEP}, {DIR}, rst={RST})
while True:
    motor.step(200)           # one revolution of a 1.8 degree motor
    print('moved 200 steps forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.step(-200)
    print('moved 200 steps back')
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Holds RST high, steps 200 forward (DIR high) then 200 back (DIR low)
